confidence_notes: I made three of the six permitted web searches. The FX search found 1 AUD = 0.6720 USD, struck at 4.00 pm on 18 November 2026. That figure came through a search summary, which said the RBA's own exchange rates page showed the same rate. I did not open the RBA page directly. The meal, coffee and beer anchors come from aggregated crowdsourced cost-of-living sites (Traveltables, Nomad Watch, citycost, MyLifeElsewhere, digital nomad guides). Those sites gave $4-8 for an inexpensive meal, $19-22 for a mid-range meal for two, $1.80-2.25 for a cappuccino, and $1.60-3.10 for domestic draught beer. Some of the data is dated, for example Traveltables was last updated in July 2023. I placed beer and the mid-range meal toward the upper end because restaurants in tourist areas like Naama Bay charge more. Direct cocktail prices were not found. The cocktail figure is an estimate based on the beer price, about 2.5 times beer at tourist bars. For wine, one undated menu excerpt listed local Omar Khayyam wine at about 250 EGP a glass, roughly $5, which I used only as a weak guide. All accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge, not live listings. Registered hostels are scarce in Sharm El Sheikh, so the hostel anchors are especially uncertain and partly based on budget guesthouse prices. July is a hot, mid-season month for international visitors but can be busy with domestic tourists. Pricing for July 2026 also carries some risk from EGP inflation and exchange-rate moves.
comparable_city_reasoning: Sharm El Sheikh is an Egyptian Red Sea resort. It costs more than Cairo or the Egypt average for restaurants and drinks served to tourists. The closest comparisons are Hurghada and Dahab, with Hurghada used for hotel price levels. Budget accommodation is less available than in Cairo or Dahab.
